Extraction-based: no headspace band. The VALUE remains a figure read-off (Figure 2D, ~150 ug/kg at 130 C; the text gives no number), which value_provenance already records.

vessel.provenance_note: WAVE B36 (2026-09-11): THE SOURCE IS ON DISK -- Ma, Fu, Cheng & Liu 2024 (Int. J. Mol. Sci. 25:8668), data/articles/Ma2024.pdf, dossier ma2024_extraction.md. Read from the print, sec. 3.2: a pilot twin-screw extruder with ten heating zones; the first five at 80, 80, 85, 90 and 100 C; this bundle's 130 C is arm (1) of the temperature series, which sets the last five to 110, 120, 130, 130 and 130 C; screw speed 150 rpm; feed 6.0 kg/h raw material plus 2.57 kg/h water; 30 % moisture; soy protein isolate : corn starch 9:1 (w/w). THE PAPER PRINTS NO RESIDENCE TIME: the 25 s below is not in the source and is an assumption, kept because a bundle is an isothermal hold and this fit row's report is frozen. B45 (2026-09-11): THE ASSUMPTION NOW HAS A MEASURED BRACKET. Unlu & Faller 2002 (J. Food Eng. 53:115, unlu2002_extraction.md) measure a twin-screw residence time distribution at THIS pot's screw speed (150 rpm) and feed rate (8.55 against 8.57 kg/h) on a machine of nearly this L/D (38.7 against 40:1): GMRT 123 s whole-barrel, one standard deviation 87-174 s. Three of Ma's ten zones are at 130 C, so on an equal-zone-length assumption the 130 C portion is about 37 s against the 25 s carried here -- the right order, about 1.5x, NOT the fourfold the reading list feared. It is an estimate and not a transfer: Unlu's feed is degermed cornmeal at 25 % moisture, not a 90 %-protein melt at 30 %, and melt viscosity sets barrel fill. The 25 s therefore STAYS, now bracketed rather than merely flagged.Figure 2D, read as an image: 130 C bar ~150 ug/kg (the scored value), 150 C ~120, 170 C ~82, and the UNEXTRUDED CONTROL ~38 ug/kg -- a starting level this bundle does not declare (named in the dossier, not acted on). ||| PRIOR NOTE, SUPERSEDED 2026-09-11 AND RETAINED AS THE AUDIT RECORD: Ma et al. 2024, Int. J. Mol. Sci. 25:8668, twin-screw extrusion of SPI + corn starch at 30 % moisture (die-zone 130 C; the bundle's 25 s is the residence time). NOT ON DISK as a PDF; the repo carries its Europe PMC full text for the directional panel (second-hand). An extruder has no fixed headspace: oxygen access is process-specific (continuous_process). Water source not applicable to a melt.

metadata.notes: Short-residence extrusion-context acrylamide benchmark. The literature point is wired through the SME-corrected effective temperature surface introduced in Priority 5.1.

model_change_note.what_changed: Nothing in this file. src/extrusion.py's SME response was DESATURATED (Wave G4, audit item 3.1): every SME quantity in that module used to be constant across the entire real 300-800 kJ/kg twin-screw window, and the temperature offset in particular hit its 40 C cap at 250 kJ/kg -- exactly this benchmark's SME. The offset is now an explicit melt energy balance dT = retained_fraction * SME / cp with a tanh soft ceiling, which at 250 kJ/kg / LME gives 18.04 C instead of 40 C. Effective temperature therefore fell 170.0 C -> 148.0 C. On the Knol 2009 lumped acrylamide anchor (Ea = 129 kJ/mol, 10.1016/j.foodchem.2009.11.049) that is a factor exp(-(Ea/R)(1/421.2 - 1/443.2)) = 0.16, i.e. 6.2x -- which is the whole of the observed move.
model_change_note.expected_miss: This benchmark is now EXPECTED TO FAIL. Predicted acrylamide 9.75 ppb against the 62.62 ppb reference: ratio 6.42x under, against an unchanged 1.5x / 0.2 dex contract. Before the desaturation it read 1.04x.
model_change_note.policy: The contract tolerance is deliberately UNCHANGED and the SME model is deliberately NOT bent back. The old 1.04x agreement was read off a saturated surface: the 40 C offset was the cap, not a computed value, so this benchmark was matching a constant rather than a model. Recovering agreement means either a real calorimetric anchor for the melt heat capacity and retained fraction (both ESTIMATED TIER, see src/extrusion.py) or a correctly SME-resolved acrylamide dataset -- not a wider tolerance.

content_correction_note.verified_against: Ma et al. 2024, Int J Mol Sci 25:8668 (PMC11354377), Figure 2D, read directly from the published figure image
corrections: acrylamide 62.62 ppb -> 150 ppb (figure_readoff). The paper reports acrylamide ONLY in Figure 2 (no table); its text says the HIGHEST acrylamide content was at 130 C, and the Fig 2D bar for 130 C reads ~150 ug/kg on a 0-160 axis. The previous 62.62 ppb matches no bar in any panel and no derivable statistic (companion Fu 2023 mean/median/geometric-mean all ruled out); its origin is unknown. The benchmark_id's 'ACSRef3' suggests the value predates the current MDPI DOI and was never re-checked against it.
uncertainty_pct 15 -> 20: a bar-chart readoff cannot support a 15% claim; 20% covers the readoff resolution plus the printed SD whiskers.

NOTE: the model_change_note above still quotes the old 62.62 reference in its expected_miss line; with the corrected 150 ppb reference the expected miss WIDENS (predicted 9.75 ppb -> ~15.4x under). The benchmark remains expected_to_fail for the same desaturation reason.

content_verification.quoted_quantification: Methods used for the extraction and separation of acrylamide were the same as Fu et al. Acrylamide quantification was performed on a UPLC-QqQ-MS/MS. Internal standard: acrylamide-2,3,3-d3.
content_verification.quoted_values: Acrylamide (ug/kg) appears only in Figure 2 (A-D); the text says 'The lowest and highest acrylamide content were found in PBMAs extruded by 20% moisture and 130 C, respectively' and gives no number.
content_verification.quantification_verdict: Isotope-dilution UPLC-MS/MS; the bundle's 150 ug/kg is a read-off of Figure 2D, not a tabulated value.
